query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the target variable itself (opened_at/closed_at derived). Directly central to explaining duration variation. Values are consistent with the timestamp columns present.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: Numeric encoding of the original priority column enables grouping/modeling duration by priority. Slightly redundant with existing priority but adds modeling leverage.

per_column.name: is_network
per_column.rationale: Binary category flag derived from short_description/category; samples (WiFi/VPN=1) are correctly grounded. Useful axis to compare durations by issue type.

per_column.name: is_database
per_column.rationale: Database flag correctly set for 'online database' row. Valid grouping dimension for duration analysis.

per_column.name: is_software
per_column.rationale: Software flag, grounded in text/category. Useful category dimension though somewhat redundant with the set of is_* flags.

per_column.name: is_hardware
per_column.rationale: Hardware flag correctly set for 'printing issues' row. Valid grouping dimension.

per_column.name: duration_category
per_column.rationale: Bucketed version of resolution_hours; largely a restatement of the target but useful for coarse grouping. Buckets match sample values correctly.

per_column.name: priority_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Group-mean duration per priority; a genuine analytical aggregate directly relevant to explaining variance by priority. Derived from in-table values.

per_column.name: category_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Group-mean duration per category; useful for attributing variance to category. Grounded in derived values.

per_column.name: duration_vs_priority_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation of a ticket's duration from its priority mean directly answers 'why durations vary'. Consistent arithmetic with the two source columns.

per_column.name: duration_vs_category_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation from category mean; a strong residual-style axis for explaining variance. Values check out arithmetically.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_duration
per_column.rationale: Mean duration per assignee, derived from assigned_to and duration. Useful to test whether assignee explains variation.

per_column.name: duration_vs_assignee_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation from assignee mean; directly relevant residual axis. Arithmetic consistent with the underlying columns.

per_column.name: has_round_duration
per_column.rationale: Constant 0 across all 500 rows, providing zero analytical leverage for explaining duration variance. Grounded but useless.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a coherent, highly relevant set for the query 'why do durations vary': the target (resolution_hours), grouping dimensions (priority, category flags, assignee) and their group means, plus residual deviation columns that directly decompose variance. Values in the row_evidence_samples are arithmetically and categorically consistent with the source text and timestamps, so groundedness is strong. Weaknesses: has_round_duration is a dead constant with no value, and duration_category is largely a restatement of the target; several is_* flags and the paired avg/deviation columns are somewhat redundant among themselves. Per scope rule, no penalty for any missing columns.
